commit.message:
Viewer: no random faults and one tick per second by default

What you see should be what you did. Random faults are opt-in with
--chaos, which uses the seed's fault configuration like the headless
simulator, and the default speed is one tick per second so messages
can be followed by eye.

files.patch:
@@ -138,15 +138,17 @@ takes faults from the keyboard: crash, restart, reboot without memory,
 partition, packet loss.
 
 ```console
-cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator --bin vsr-simulator-tui -- --lite --quiet
-cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator --bin vsr-simulator-tui -- 10693013600028533629 --until 40000
+cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator --bin vsr-simulator-tui -- --lite
+cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator --bin vsr-simulator-tui -- --chaos 10693013600028533629 --until 40000
 ```
 
-`--quiet` turns the random faults off so what you see is what you did;
-`--until` runs at full speed to a tick and pauses there, for stepping into a
-failure a seed reproduces. On quit it prints the seed and every fault you
-injected as a script, and `--script FILE` replays one, so a scenario found
-by hand becomes a reproducible run.
+By default nothing goes wrong unless you make it: the network is reliable
+and only the faults you inject happen, at one tick per second. `--chaos`
+uses the seed's random faults like the headless simulator, and `--until`
+runs at full speed to a tick and pauses there, for stepping into a failure
+a seed reproduces. On quit it prints the seed and every fault you injected
+as a script, and `--script FILE` replays one, so a scenario found by hand
+becomes a reproducible run.
